condition: expanding painful raised chest keloid scar growing beyond a 9-month-old skin piercing site
level_rationale: A painful thick raised scar growing past the original puncture border 9 months after a chest skin piercing in a 22-year-old with dark brown skin indicates an actively expanding anterior-chest keloid requiring dermatologist evaluation for intralesional corticosteroid or multimodal scar therapy, whereas a tiny flat healed scar confined to the piercing hole 9 months after a chest skin piercing represents normal mature wound healing requiring only routine self-care.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 22 with dark brown skin, chest skin piercing 9 months ago, and painful thick raised scar growing beyond the piercing site) without naming the diagnosis, with an exact 20-vs-20 word span swap and identical digit multisets across all 6 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rule A first choice, changing only scar morphology in f3 on the same 9-month chest piercing to 'a tiny flat healed scar at' shifts care cleanly from dermatologist keloid therapy (level 3) to self-care (level 1) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
